issues.description: validate_conda returns True for empty string, conflating 'unset' with 'valid'
issues.detail: The early `if conda_executable == '': return True` makes the predicate lie: callers cannot distinguish 'no path provided' from 'path validated as a working conda'. Combined with the kernelspec fallback, a user who ticks custom_conda but leaves the path empty will see a green-light preferences page and then a 'conda not found' error at kernel start. Either return False on empty (forcing the user to fill it in), gate save-time on a non-empty path, or move the empty-string acceptance into the caller behind a separate is_set predicate.

issues.description: Substring match on --version output is too permissive to identify conda-family tools
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'])` is a free-form substring scan: 'mamba' is a substring of 'micromamba', and any binary whose --version output happens to mention 'conda' (wrappers, anaconda-* tools, help banners) will pass. The right shape is to parse the first whitespace token of the version string and compare for equality against a known set, or anchor a regex to the version number.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the file browser breaks the picker on macOS and Linux
issues.detail: conda/mamba/micromamba on POSIX systems have no `.exe` suffix; the file dialog will hide every valid candidate on the platforms where most conda users live. The feature exists precisely to support non-standard install locations, where the binary is most often extensionless. Branch on sys.platform for the filter (or drop the filter and rely on validate_conda).

issues.description: validate_conda executes a user-supplied binary with no timeout, on the UI thread
issues.detail: `run_program(conda_executable, ['--version']).communicate()` will block indefinitely if the user points at a hung or interactive binary. The validation runs in the preferences dialog on the UI thread, so a misbehaving path can wedge the dialog. Add a `communicate(timeout=...)`, kill on TimeoutExpired, and document that the predicate executes the file as a side effect.

issues.description: create_browsefile / create_lineedit gain validate_callback and validate_reason with no documented contract
issues.detail: Two new keyword arguments are forwarded into create_lineedit with no docstring update on either factory. The semantics — when the callback is invoked, what argument it receives, what its return value means, how validate_reason is surfaced, whether it must accept empty input — are left for future readers to reverse-engineer from call sites. State the precondition/postcondition in a docstring so future callers don't each invent their own empty-string ambiguity.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() in select_file is an unrelated behavior change to a shared widget helper
issues.detail: `select_file` is used by every browsefile in Spyder; adding `edit.setFocus()` after a file is chosen changes its contract for all callers as a side effect of a conda-only feature. If focus-after-pick is needed to trigger validate_callback on focus-out for the conda field, wire it at that call site or justify it for every caller. Otherwise this belongs in its own patch with its own justification.

issues.description: kernelspec.argv reaches across module boundaries via string config keys instead of a single resolver
issues.detail: argv() now reads `conda_path` and `custom_conda` from the main_interpreter section via untyped string keys, re-deriving 'the user's chosen conda' inline. The two-key state (boolean toggle + path) encodes one fact and invites drift (True with empty path, False with stale path). Decompose: a single `resolve_conda_executable()` in spyder/utils/conda.py that consults configuration and returns an optional path, with the invariant tying custom_conda and conda_path enforced in one place.

issues.description: No tests for validate_conda or the kernelspec custom-conda fallback branch
issues.detail: validate_conda is a pure predicate with obvious cases (empty, missing file, non-executable, wrong tool, right tool) and is trivially testable. The kernelspec fallback (custom_conda enabled vs disabled, conda_path set vs empty, find_conda succeeds vs fails) is the whole point of the PR. Neither is exercised by a test in this diff, despite the failure mode being 'kernels won't start'.

issues.description: Decision to consult custom conda only when find_conda() fails contradicts the UI text
issues.detail: The new code only uses the user's custom conda when `find_conda()` returns falsy. The checkbox is labeled 'Use a custom Conda/Mamba/Micromamba executable' with a tooltip saying 'instead of finding the executable from the interpreter path' — but the implementation treats custom as a fallback, not an override. A user who explicitly configures custom because auto-detection picks the wrong binary will be silently ignored. Either check custom_conda first (override semantics) or change the UI text to 'as a fallback'.

issues.description: Nested ternary in kernelspec.argv is harder to read than an equivalent if-block
issues.detail: The fallback chain nests a ternary inside an assignment inside an `if not conda_exe`, spanning seven lines. The data is simple: 'custom path if enabled, else None'. Two lines — `custom_enabled = self.get_conf(...)` and `conda_exe = self.get_conf('conda_path', ...) if custom_enabled else None` before the guard — read better and match the file's voice.

issues.description: out.decode() uses default encoding and bare except swallows decode/exit failures silently
issues.detail: Decoding subprocess output with no encoding argument can raise UnicodeDecodeError on hostile binaries or non-UTF-8 locales, and the bare `except Exception` returns False with no signal. Prefer `out.decode(errors='replace')` and narrow the except to the specific failure modes you want to swallow, so real bugs aren't silently rebranded as 'not a conda'.

issues.description: No trimming or normalization of user-entered path before validation
issues.detail: The textbox value is fed directly to `os.path.isfile` and `os.access` with no `expanduser`, `strip()`, or quote-stripping. Pasted paths on Windows often arrive surrounded by double quotes; users routinely paste paths with leading/trailing whitespace or `~`. A two-line `os.path.expanduser(path.strip().strip('"'))` removes a class of false-negative validation failures.

issues.description: validate_conda mixes early-return and a 'valid' flag with inconsistent exit discipline
issues.detail: In one short function the author uses three exit disciplines: early `return True/False` guards, a mutable `valid` flag set inside a try, and a `return False` in a bare except. The invariant the `valid` flag is supposed to maintain is unstated, and a reader must simulate the function to know what it returns. Express the predicate as a clean sequence of guarded returns or as a single Boolean expression over named subchecks.

issues.description: os.access(..., os.X_OK) is unreliable on Windows and adds little value over the run_program check
issues.detail: On Windows os.access with X_OK essentially checks existence; on POSIX it can lie under ACLs and NFS. The actual validator is the run_program/--version call below. The X_OK gate does nothing useful on Windows and can falsely reject on some POSIX configurations — drop it and let the subprocess call be the gate.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly on a NEEDS-WORK verdict. The feature design is sensible — a checkbox plus a path, persisted to config, consulted in argv() when auto-discovery fails — but `validate_conda` is the weak joint: it returns True for empty input (conflating unset with valid), identifies conda-family tools by loose substring match on --version output, executes a user-supplied binary with no timeout, and braids early returns with a `valid` flag. The `filters='*.exe'` filter unanimously breaks the picker on macOS and Linux, the very platforms the feature is most needed on. Three reviewers separately note that the two-key (custom_conda + conda_path) state should be resolved through a single conda-resolver abstraction rather than reached for by string keys in kernelspec.argv, and every reviewer flags the unrelated `edit.setFocus()` change to the shared select_file helper as scope creep. No tests accompany the new validator or the kernelspec fallback branch. Fix the validator's contract, fix the file filter, document validate_callback's semantics, and split out the focus change, and this is mergeable.
